subject.title: Org claim: vmware-aiops + vmware-monitor — @kingaiwork lookalikes impersonate @zw008 listings (same pattern as #2966/#3035)

question: Does the evidence justify hiding the two `@kingaiwork` VMware listings only, or does the repeated confirmed pattern justify broader action against the publisher account?
rationale: The repository provides the enforcement tools, but determining impersonation and the proportional scope of enforcement requires staff access to stored listing evidence, moderation history, and account-wide context.

options.title: Hide both listings and review account
options.body: Confirm the copied-content evidence, hide the two disputed listings immediately, then perform a separate scoped review of the publisher's remaining catalog.

options.title: Hide only these listings
options.body: Resolve the two reported resources without broader account action if staff cannot establish a sufficiently consistent account-wide abuse pattern.

options.title: Request more evidence
options.body: Leave the listings unchanged temporarily and ask for exact inspect output only if stored versions do not confirm the public fingerprints.

recommendation.title: Hide both listings and review account
recommendation.body: Confirm the copied-content evidence, hide the two disputed listings immediately, then perform a separate scoped review of the publisher's remaining catalog.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the active org-claim policy RFC and is the strongest available routing candidate for a staff namespace and enforcement-scope decision.
